solved.topic: Nuclear radius and density - ratio for two nuclei
solved.q: Find the ratio of the radii of nuclei with mass numbers A1 = 27 and A2 = 125.
steps: Given: A1 = 27, A2 = 125. Formula: R = R0 A^(1/3).
Answer: R2/R1 = 5/3 = 1.67 (no units, it is a ratio).

solved.q: The density of nuclear matter is 2.3 x 10^17 kg/m^3 and mass of a nucleon is 1.67 x 10^-27 kg. Estimate the value of R0 in R = R0 A^(1/3).
steps: Formula: rho = mass/volume = (A mN) / ((4/3) pi R^3), and R = R0 A^(1/3) so R^3 = R0^3 A.
Substituting: rho = (A mN) / ((4/3) pi R0^3 A) = 3 mN / (4 pi R0^3).
Numerator = 5.01 x 10^-27. Denominator = 4 x 3.14 x 2.3 x 10^17 = 28.9 x 10^17.
solved.ans: R0 is approximately 1.2 x 10^-15 m (1.2 fm)

solved.topic: Mass defect and binding energy of Helium-4
solved.q: Calculate the mass defect and binding energy per nucleon for Helium-4 nucleus. Given: mass of proton = 1.007825 u, mass of neutron = 1.008665 u, mass of He-4 nucleus = 4.002603 u, 1 u = 931.5 MeV.
steps: Formula: delta m = [Z mp + (A-Z) mn] - M.
Binding energy E = delta m x 931.5 = 0.030377 x 931.5 = 28.3 MeV.
Binding energy per nucleon = 28.3 / 4 = 7.07 MeV per nucleon.
solved.ans: delta m = 0.0304 u, Binding energy = 28.3 MeV, BE per nucleon = 7.07 MeV

solved.q: A radioactive substance has a half-life of 5 years. Calculate its decay constant in SI units.
steps: Given: T(1/2) = 5 years = 5 x 365 x 24 x 3600 s.

solved.topic: Fraction of radioactive sample remaining after n half-lives
solved.q: A radioactive sample initially has a mass of 800 g and a half-life of 10 days. Find the mass remaining after 40 days.
steps: Given: N0 (mass) = 800 g, T(1/2) = 10 days, t = 40 days.
Number of half-lives n = t / T = 40/10 = 4.

solved.q: A radioactive source has an initial activity of 8000 disintegrations per minute and a half-life of 15 minutes. Find its activity after 45 minutes.
steps: Given: A0 = 8000 dis/min, T(1/2) = 15 min, t = 45 min.
Formula: A = A0 (1/2)^(t/T), since activity falls in the same way as N.

solved.q: Calculate the energy released in the alpha decay of U-238 to Th-234. Given masses: M(U-238) = 238.05079 u, M(Th-234) = 234.04363 u, M(He-4) = 4.00260 u, 1 u = 931.5 MeV.
steps: Formula: Q = [M(U-238) - M(Th-234) - M(He-4)] c^2, with 1 u = 931.5 MeV giving energy directly.

solved.topic: Number of nuclei from activity and decay constant
solved.q: A radioactive source of Cobalt-60 (half-life 5.3 years) has an activity of 3.7 x 10^10 disintegrations per second (1 curie). Find the number of Co-60 nuclei present.
steps: Given: T(1/2) = 5.3 years, Activity A = 3.7 x 10^10 s^-1.
Convert half-life to seconds: T(1/2) = 5.3 x 365 x 24 x 3600 s = 1.672 x 10^8 s.
Formula: A = lambda N, so N = A / lambda.
